answer: Conviction-weighted voting makes identity cheap but influence expensive. Each vote gains weight slowly, the way marble gains its veins crystal by crystal; a newcomer reaches power only after long participation. Splitting stake across a hundred sybil puppets backfires: every puppet restarts its own curve, so N identities multiply nothing — the attacker waits N periods for less influence than one identity. Even an ember of locked stake on each puppet cannot be double-counted: conviction accrues per identity, not per wallet, so farming dilutes influence while the attacker's stake stays frozen.
